summary:
## Key Concepts

- **Local AI / Ownership**
  - Running models on your own hardware keeps data private; no vendor can access your info.
  - Local models are free per-token and work offline, making them ideal for sensitive or regulated workloads.

> [!TIP] Keep a mixture: use local models for private data and cloud models for peak performance or fresh web info.

- **Hermes Operating System**
  - Hermes OS centralizes conversations, memories, personas, goals, and connectors (e.g., GitHub).
  - It can orchestrate multiple models and pipelines so you see your entire AI ecosystem in one place.

> [!NOTE] Hermes benefits from models with large context windows for memory-heavy agent tasks.

- **Ollama + Open Source Models**
  - Ollama provides an easy local model manager to download and run open-source models like Quen, Mistral, Gemma.
  - Models are typically ~1 year behind frontier cloud models but improve rapidly.

- **Model Selection and Context Window**
  - Hermes Agent requires models with ~64k token context to fully support its memory features.
  - For Hermes integration, prefer models like **Quen 3 Coder 30B (64K)**; smaller models are fine for short tasks.

> [!IMPORTANT] Performance scales with your machine. Larger models may be slow; choose models that match your hardware.

- **Modes and Trade-offs**
  - **Vault Mode**: Fully local, private—use for client data, health records, proprietary code.
  - **Connected/Performance Mode**: Use cloud models for faster, higher-quality or web-aware answers.
  - Toggle dynamically per task so privacy and performance trade-offs are explicit.

- **Practical Advice & Compliance**
  - Download, test, and remove models to find what works; expect friction when first configuring.
  - Local models are useful for compliance (SOC 2, GDPR, ISO) and regulated environments.

## Takeaways

- Learn to run and manage local models with Ollama, integrate them into Hermes OS, and pick the right mode per task.
- Local-first workflows protect data, reduce costs, and provide offline capability—while cloud models remain valuable for peak tasks.
- Investing time now in local AI skills will pay off as on-device models approach frontier capability within a year.
